adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. In JS, `z.string()` is an object and `.toString()` yields `"[object Object]"`, so both computed keys collapse to the same literal property name and the latter overrides the former. As a result, the schema does not actually accept arbitrary numeric “expiry” fields (e.g. `expiry_date`, `expires_in`) nor arbitrary extra fields; with Zod `z.object({...})` defaulting to stripping unknown keys, `safeParse(response)` will silently drop all unrecognized properties and keep essentially only `access_token` (plus the meaningless `"[object Object]"` if present). This matches the finding’s claim of silent data loss when the code path `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is taken.
